speaker: Mikel Arteta
quote_text:
Hi everyone, if you have a question, raise your  hand and we'll come to you. Cameras are already  
at the back. We'll start with Nick at the back  here. Nick, hello. Hello. A fairy tale comeback  
with a worrying knock for Gabriel. Yes, I think a  beautiful moment to see how much our people love,  
respect, and admire Bukayo. And it's not a  surprise to any of us. And I think the best  
example is his reaction. Immediately after scoring  a goal, what does he do? He goes and says thank  
you for all the hard work that all the sports  science guys, physios, and everybody involved  
in the recovery has done for him to be able to do  in the condition that he did. So I think he lifted  
the stadium, the energy, and I'm grateful to have  him back. How is he feeling after this? Yeah,  
he was very positive, everything. The first one  is always the one, how am I going to feel? Because  
now I have different opposition in front of me,  different demands, and the pressure, and he dealt  
with it really well. And as you said, the downside  to that is Gabi and Jurrien, that we don't know  
how they're going to be. We will be assessing them  tomorrow and understand better probably how we are  
with those two. What were your early impressions,  Mikel, on Gabi? It looked like a hamstring. Is  
that...? With both of them, because there are two  players in this team that never want to come off  
are those two probably. So Gabi felt something  in his hamstring. We don't know how big that is,  
and with Jurrien as well. He already was  struggling very early in the game. He managed  
to continue. At some point he couldn't. So that's  a downside to it. So Jurrien was a hamstring? No,  
Jurrien wasn't. Yeah. I mean, they've been so  important for you defensively, haven't they?  
And clearly, you know, after about a week, I mean,  it's, you know, it feels... The good thing is that  
it's been like this the whole season. I mean, you  see Martinelli today, you say we miss him in three  
months. You see Bukayo four months, Kai four  months, Gabi Jesus almost the whole season, you  
know. How we have managed to be where we are with  all those injuries, Ben White hasn't participated  
at all this season is what it is, that we want it  so much that we're going to give it a real go, and  
we are very excited for the next week. Alex, you  just touched on it, the issues at the attacking  
end of the pitch, and now having the selection  issues in defence? How much of a worry is that  
with the game, Edson so close, and then and then  Rea on shoot? Well, you can imagine we lose four  
players in the defensive line in one week, so  Calafiori, Ben White, Jurrien, and Gabi Magalhaes,  
we have still another four that they are so bloody  willing that they will do the job. You mentioned  
right at the start that obviously went to all  the fitness guys and on the camera we could see  
him hugging Sam Wilson. I was just wondering if  you could talk about how important Sam and people  
like Sam as well are in those kind of weeks coming  up to players coming back to fitness. Listen, as  
a manager, I think being part of the staff, we all  love this kind of recognition and gestures because  
it goes behind the professional side of it and  there is a connection there that is so necessary  
and to be able to appreciate as well the amount  of work and stress as well and responsibility  
that they have to go through because they will  be like this. I hope everything goes well and the  
work that we've done is going to work. So I was  very pleased with that. Because I take it there's  
probably a lot of times where it's just those two  alone at the training ground together when maybe  
he's getting back on the grass and kind of...  Yeah, and that's why the emotional part is so  
important, because you can do all the physical  work and all the conditioning, but you need to  
live the players. Four months is a long time,  and there are moments that, yeah, we travel and  
we go to play Champions League, and you are there  for two days, you're on your own on the training  
ground, and it's not easy. Tom for Polando. I  think that could get swallowed up in Saka and the  
injuries, but Mikel Merino scored, I think it's  his fifth goal in eight games as playing a centre  
forward. That must really please you, knowing  this is playing out of position. He does, yeah,  
but he's got that capacity to score goals, to  sense the danger and to move in the right moments  
into the right spaces. Today was a different goal,  but then you ask him to play as an eight and he  
does it perfectly and understands the timing, the  position, the role is so good. It's a joke to have  
players like this. I saw Ethan as well, he had  some really good moments. Martinelli, I think,  
was superb as well, as you see how much we missed  him, you know, that threat, that attacking purpose  
that he has every time he's on the ball. So some  good performances. Okay, last couple, James ESPN.  
You mentioned obviously had to deal with injuries  all season. Have you ever known a season like  
this? No, unfortunately, no, especially because  as well they've been some big, big players and  
in very, very critical positions, you know, and  affecting the whole length. But we have some a  
lot of good news as well, so look at Myles, look  at Ethan, look at all the players doing all the  
stuff, so… That's it. Just how hard has it been  to plan and strategise when you lose players?  
Yeah, you're scratching your head and now in the  next few games the same. But at the same time,  
it's been a great learning experience, you know,  for us and all the coaches and the staff to manage  
that situation. And at the end, the players are  going to react to how we react to it. You just  
have to feel sorry for yourself and say, it's  impossible, how are we going to do this? It  
will be impossible, but this group, these boys,  they don't give you the reason to act like that,  
and look where we are, and we are in April.  And finally, Jorgenson. This could now be a  
really massive week for Jakub Kiwior. He hasn't  played much football, but just how confident are  
you that you can throw him in against the likes of  Mario and Madrid? Yeah. Well, the good thing with  
Jakub is that he's been very reliable. Every time  we need him, he's always there, he's available,  
and he does his job. We ask him to play as a left  centre back, as a right centre back, as a left  
full back. So he's ready. He was with a smile  on his face. You know, he's sad for Gabi, but  
he really wanted to play as well and he will be  fine. Do you think he'll be up for the challenge  
of coming up against some of the best strikers in  the world? Well, if you ask the dressing room how  
much they want to play the next two games and the  Real Madrid game, believe me, everybody wants to  
be on that pitch. Okay, guys, thanks very much.  Thank you. Can I just check what's going on?
title: Mikel Arteta post-match press conference | Arsenal 2-1 Fulham
